current.text: He joined the Denver Nuggets this offseason.

He is expected to come off the bench for Denver behind starters Jamal Murray, Christian Braun, Cam Johnson, Aaron Gordon and Nikola Jokic. Experts expect him to get the most bench minutes but in a smaller role than last season.
Experts worry about how his game fits during the minutes he shares with Jokic.

His upside case: one injury to Braun or Johnson could push him to about 32 minutes, 19 points and five assists. One expert also expects Denver to move Cam Johnson by the trade deadline, which would open the same role.
Experts agree he is not a top 100 player this season. His fair value is around rank 135 to 140, and taking him at an ESPN top 100 price is a bad pick.
Denver plays 43 games through March 28 and has only 14 back-to-backs, one of the lowest counts in the league.

durable.text: He is a great scorer. Teams must adjust for him on both ends because of his spacing and defensive limitations.
Good FT% on solid volume is his best category, and he keeps turnovers low for a scorer.
He makes very few threes and grabs few rebounds for a forward.

note: Yahoo and ESPN both rank him 102. The experts see him closer to rank 135 to 140, which sits at the very end of our 144-player pool. He is worth 1 to 3 USD (Yahoo average cost 1.5, ESPN 1.9), well below the 10 USD our league paid last season. He fits punt 3PM or punt REB builds that want points, FT% and low turnovers. Early in the season, check whether his minutes hold near 29 off the bench, and watch Braun's and Cam Johnson's health and any trade of them, since that is his path back to a starter's role.
